project.lead: A project is a folder where the AI works, together with the rules for working there (the project policy).
project.policyNote: The AI changes files without asking. Write here what it should ask you about first, and it is given to every AI in this project. The example is fine to start with.
project.policyStart:
## About this project
- The code and documents in the working folder are what this project is about. Follow the rules already there (README, AGENTS.md and the like) and the way things are written.

## Ask the user first
- For a change that affects how something looks or feels to use, show a sample and ask before building it.
- Ask before starting work that changes direction or will take a long time.
- Get approval before publishing, sending anything to outside services or people, replacing a running service, doing anything that costs money, or deleting something that cannot be restored.

## Decide without asking
- For anything not listed above, decide without asking, go ahead, and report the result.

## How to work
- Except for small fixes, when the work is done, have the work checked by an AI other than the one that made it, fix what it finds, and then ask the user to review it.
- For a screen design change, have a separate AI create each candidate, up to three in total. The owner shows them to the user together and asks which one they prefer. When asking, the owner also says which one it recommends and why.

## Not allowed
- Do not write secrets such as API keys or passwords in records or deliverables.

alpacawork-betterquality.title: Criteria set first, then another AI checks
alpacawork-betterquality.what: Before building, the AI sets the criteria for passing and compares options for decisions with a large impact. An AI other than the one that built the result checks the real thing, and it is fixed before you are asked to review it. This takes more time and tokens (light work is only checked by the AI itself).
alpacawork-betterquality.when: when planning, when asking for a review, and when receiving findings

askmeclearly.title: Shorter, easier-to-read questions and reports
askmeclearly.what: The AI uses images or video to show where to look, so you can decide or check right away.
askmeclearly.when: when asking the user to decide, and when writing a report

doyourjob.title: Fewer questions for you
doyourjob.what: The AI goes ahead on its own with what it can find out and what it may decide, and asks you only what you alone can decide.
doyourjob.when: before asking the user, and before making a choice with large consequences
